items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: There are others like Gil Evans, I’ll put Max in that, Duke Ellington was definitely in that category. He could tolerate any kind of crazy behavior because he knew what he wanted out of those musicians.

ctx.x: I love this comment you made about when you had, it might have been M’Boom that you were talking about or some of the other large ensembles, but you said something about, “Everyone has a different idea of where the beat is at.” And I can imagine that’s got to be a little tricky.

Well that was because see there’s a certain ego about drummers. And they all have to be right when they’re in the position of propelling a band. You know the drummer has to be the most constant figure because everybody else can match that. It’s the most audible sound and everybody can feel that vibration so they can lock in to that. But when you have six or seven drummers who are all, I mean all these guys were great musicians, you know, Max had chosen us from his observations and experience with us. Not every…

that we all had so much respect for Max Roach that we just let him lead everything. But when we started presenting our own music, and you might have to criticize Max Roach for something, then you wonder how that’s going to go. But see he was broad enough where he could accept that you know. Now not all leaders can accept criticism of themselves for whatever they do. So they’re locked in a position where if they’re going over a cliff they’re gone. You know. And if you don’t like it just get off the cliff. I mean…
